findings.detail: The site-by-site exposure table updated the two changed sites to '601 (now :605)' and '693 (now :699)', but left the other four rows at 643 / 738 / 790 / 803. The comments added above the two fixed calls shifted those lines: the styled builders now sit at 647 (changeLogData, chunked), 744 (changeLogData, single), 796 (summaryData) and 809 (supplierData). The same stale set is repeated in docs/quality/tech-debt-register.md:13 ('the styled one at 643/738/790/803'). This matters more than usual here because the register explicitly hands those four line numbers to a future reader as the latent trap to watch, and the final commit of this branch claims to have fixed audit line numbers — so a reader will reasonably trust them and land on the wrong lines.
findings.summary: Four of the six FileValidationTab line refs are now stale

findings.detail: The two sibling assertions in this describe carry explanatory messages ('exportData carries source rows, so a Date reaches this call…' and a comment on the length-2 guard), but `expect(styled).toHaveLength(4)` has only a preceding comment. This is the assertion most likely to trip on a legitimate change — consolidating the chunked and single export paths, or dropping the supplier sheet, moves the count without introducing any defect — and when it does, the failure a future author sees is a bare 'expected length 4, received 3' with no hint that the correct response is to redo the exposure analysis in the audit rather than to bump the number.
findings.summary: The styled-builder count guard fires without an explanation message
